result:
I found and fixed 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings. After the fix, I checked all 150 rules against a reference implementation built from each docstring and the module's shared rules. I tried roughly 1,400 quantity/unit-price combinations plus the negative-input error, and nothing disagreed.

**What I fixed:**

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 07, 141, 142 | The cap was applied to the price before the discount was calculated (`min(base, cap) * pct`) | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 133 | Same problem on a marginal rule (`min((qty-5)*unit, cap) * pct`) | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 16, 105 | The discount started at 101 units, not at the documented 100+ | Changed the condition to `qty >= 100` |
| 37 | The discount started at 6 units, not at the documented 5+ | Changed the condition to `qty >= 5` |
| 19, 92 | `round()` was used, which can round up | Changed to floor (`// 100`) |
| 111, 124 | Documented as marginal, but the discount was taken on the whole amount | Changed to `(qty - threshold) * unit * pct // 100` |
| 125 | The rate was 6%, but the docstring says 5% | Changed to 5% |

Rules 22, 26, 30, 33, 38, 43, 66, 70, 85 and 118 are written differently from the rest (`if disc > cap`, `20 <= qty`, `not qty < 12`, and so on), but they behave the same as their docstrings, so I left them alone. I made no other changes to the file.

STATUS: DONE
